todos.context: User preferences (sort order, sort direction, tag overlay visibility) are already persisted through fyne Preferences in internal/gui/app/settings.go, but there is no UI to view or change them. Dialogs are registered and lifecycle-managed via the dialogKind enum and dialogManager in internal/gui/app/dialogs.go; the closest existing patterns are internal/gui/ui/help.go (read-only info dialog) and internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go (interactive dialog with its own key handling). Keyboard shortcuts are wired in internal/gui/ui/shortcuts.go and the remembered settings and key list are documented in CLAUDE.md.

plan.summary: A settings window holding four switches - show the tag overlay, autosave the XMP sidecar, autosave the JPEG packet, show the Save button - opened with the I key, which until now toggled the overlay. The switches live beside the other preferences in internal/gui/app/settings.go and are applied live; the tags dialog gets one Save button in place of Save JPEG, shown only while at least one autosave is off, and the automatic sidecar and JPEG writes in tags_action.go and tags_runs.go obey the two autosave switches.

steps.title: Preference layer for the three new switches
steps.details: Add keys autoSaveXMP (default true), autoSaveJPEG (default false) and showSaveButton (default true), the matching Application fields, a restoreSaveSettings called next to restoreTagVisibility in Run, and one saver per switch in the style of saveTagVisibility. Add the pure rule saveButtonVisible(show, autoXMP, autoJPEG) = show && !(autoXMP && autoJPEG) with a table test beside TestNormalizeSortOrder.

steps.title: Settings dialog widget
steps.details: NewSettingsDialog(opts, window, callbacks) built like ui.NewHelp: a VBox of four widget.Check rows and a Close button. Every check applies at once. The Save-button check is disabled and unchecked while both autosave checks are on. Test the enable/disable rule and the callbacks.

steps.title: Wire the window into the app
steps.details: Add dialogSettings to dialogKind and handleSettings, which opens and closes it exactly like handleHelp. Its callbacks flip the Application fields, save them and apply - the overlay one keeps the body of handleToggleTags. Rename OnToggleTags to OnSettings in ShortcutCallbacks, bind glfw.KeyI to it, and change the I row in the help dialog to Settings.

steps.title: One Save button in the tags dialog
steps.details: Rename saveJPEGBtn/OnSaveJPEG to saveBtn/OnSave, label it Save, and build it for every photo rather than only for a JPEG. Add TagsDialogOptions.ShowSave and leave the button out when it is false. The session's saveJPEG becomes save: it always writes the sidecar and, for a JPEG, the packet. The dialog is built with ShowSave from saveButtonVisible.

steps.title: Gate the automatic writes on the settings
steps.details: With autoSaveXMP off, close and runFinished write no sidecar - close still calls tagRuns.takeOver so a re-attached dialog gets its fields back - and finishDetached/saveTyped only fill the cache, the overlay and the notification before releasing the run. With autoSaveJPEG on, the same two moments also write the JPEG packet of a JPEG photo, in the dialog path and in the detached run path. Extend the existing table tests with the off/on combinations.

steps.title: Documentation
steps.details: Update the Features section (settings window, the two autosave switches, the Save button rule), the stock-tags paragraph (the sidecar is no longer written unconditionally on close) and the shortcut list (I = Settings).

questions.question: What does the I key do once the settings window exists?
questions.answer: It opens the settings window; the tag overlay is toggled by a checkbox there.

questions.question: What does autosave XMP = off mean?
questions.answer: The sidecar is written only by the Save button; closing the tags dialog writes nothing.

questions.question: What shape does the save button in the tags dialog take?
questions.answer: One Save button replacing Save JPEG: it writes the sidecar and, for a JPEG, the packet.

questions.question: Is "show the Save button" a setting of its own?
questions.answer: Yes, a checkbox, greyed out and forced off while both autosaves are on.

questions.question: With autosave XMP off, what happens to a backgrounded generation that lands with no dialog?
questions.answer: Cache, overlay and notification only - no file is written.

questions.question: When does autosave JPEG write?
questions.answer: At the same moments as the sidecar: after a generation and on close.

risks: The handover between a closing dialog and a running generation is delicate: with autosave off nobody writes, so takeOver must still run for the re-attach to restore the fields.
The cache means "the file holds these tags"; filling it without writing is a deliberate exception, so the Save button must never short-circuit on equality.
An automatic JPEG write rewrites the file when the XMP packet is too small, and the Sony Recover Image DB note must still reach the user from that path.
I changes meaning: the help dialog, CLAUDE.md and any test naming OnToggleTags must follow.

todos.description: Replace the folder browser with a saved list of folders for quick access.
todos.context: The left panel currently embeds a GoLand-style directory tree (ui.DirTree, a fyne widget.Tree over library.Scanner): FileBrowser constructs it in NewFileBrowser, lays it out in build() next to the "Open Folder..." button, and exposes SetRoot/OpenPath which Application calls from handleChooseFolder and the startup restore in internal/gui/app/app.go (the last root is already persisted through fyne Preferences). This task replaces that tree with a saved/bookmarked folder list for quick access; the saved list would be persisted with the other preference keys in internal/gui/app/settings.go and would fire the existing OnDirectorySelected callback. There are no dirtree/filebrowser tests yet - sibling widget tests in internal/gui/ui/ show the testing style - and CLAUDE.md documents the current left-panel tree behaviour.
